Iceland Faces Widespread Disruption as General Strike Halts Key Services

Reykjavik—A nationwide general strike has brought economic activity across Iceland to a near-standstill, with transportation, retail, and public services all severely affected. The walkout, which began early Tuesday morning, is ongoing and has already caused significant disruption to both domestic and international operations.

Among the companies impacted is Isavia Ohf, Iceland’s airport and air navigation operator. International flights at Keflavik and Akureyri airports have faced extensive delays and cancellations, stranding hundreds of travelers and forcing airlines to adjust schedules. “We are doing everything possible to support passengers during this difficult period, but our capacity is severely limited,” said Isavia Ohf spokesperson Sigríður Jónsdóttir.

The Confederation of Icelandic Labor Unions estimates that as many as 65,000 workers have joined the strike, affecting not only airports but also the banking, healthcare, education, and retail sectors. Supermarkets and petrol stations in Reykjavik and Akureyri reported shortages of staff and restricted opening hours. “Supply chains are under immense strain,” said Björn Einarsson, an analyst at the Icelandic Chamber of Commerce. “If the strike continues, we may see more pronounced impacts on the availability of essential goods.”

Union leaders say the strike is in response to stalled wage negotiations and rising inflation, which reached 7.1% in May. “Workers are demanding fair compensation in line with cost-of-living increases,” said Elín Magnúsdóttir, a union representative, at a rally outside Parliament.

The government has called for urgent talks, but as of Wednesday afternoon, there has been no breakthrough. Analysts warn that prolonged industrial action could further dampen growth prospects for Iceland’s economy in 2024.
